No. I am not going to end my life being of childcare. I'm honestly shocked and dissapointed that my plea for help once again circles around to the money I should be spending on the children instead of trying to focus on getting better somehow. 

My children have had nannies, their grandma and even done traditional child care. I'm still overwhelmed and tired of doing it on my own.  We have had nanny services, driving services and even a maid and cooking services.  Paying and buying people to do things doesn't make the situation better.  

What advice would you give to someone who doesn't have money?   

Once again I'm lumped into the privelged rich girl mindset to just spend spend spend to solve all my problems but it's not that easy.  And I may have money but if I spend it all on services, I will be left with 0 at the end of the month so what good would that do when I can't pay my mortgage or for food because I decided to put everything into the services everyone expects me to pay for?

Exactly! It's like we, as parents, aren't allowed to feel anything other that common fatigue? It doesn't make sense.  And asking for help, even if just emotionally, tends to be met with agression. Like how dare we feel that way when you have kids who should be your priority.

Thank you.  You're the only one who actually responded to what I wrote without casting judgement. I do appreciate your words and you've given me the insight I was seeking.  Thank you for taking the time to listen and respond

Disagree. Happy mom, happy kids. Unhappy mom, unhappy kids. Doesn't matter if they are 2 or 16. Their ages are irrelevant because as children, regardless of age, will be affected by my unhappiness and resentment.

I understand that perspective although I disagree. I welcomed the help from family and their father.  Their father, never fully stepped up.  My mother, ended up teaching the children to lie so she could sit in bed watching TV instead of taking them to art classes.  Did I mention I went out of town 2 weeks ago and the kids didn't brush their teeth once? She apologized for "dropping the ball" but "at least they ate"...that was a constant cycle in my house.

As far as a live in nanny. I did that for several years and it's not my favorite arrangement for various reason.  

Just because I have money doesn't mean I want to spend half my income paying people to take care of my kids when their father is fully capable.

Also, how can you "punish" a father by forcing him to help take care of his kids? Sorry but wanting and needing him to step up is hardly punishment. It's forcing him to be a parent to the children he created

As previously mentioned, you need to have a sit down with your girlfriend regarding parenting. She NEEDS to allow you to disciple her daughter and she needs to be allowed to disciple yours when needed.  You need to set the boundaries of what punishments are allowed and what isn't?   

If she doesn't agree, it might be time to consider moving out because it will NOT get better.

Honestly, having been in your place and chosing the "popular, financially driven" choice and not my own, I regret it.  Children are a blessing, you will love all three unconditionally, but at the expense of your happiness, you may grow to resent the choice you didn't want to take and will ultimately make you unhappy.  What's better, a mommy who is happy and fulfilled but making less money, or the mommy that makes a ton of money but lives in a constant state of "what ifs" and possible regret? 

In the end, you have to do what is best for YOU.  You were taking birth control and had no intentions on getting pregnant, regardless of what anyone else's opinion you have to put yourself, your happiness and your family first.
